page: Amazon Web Services m9gd.48xlarge is a high-scale general-purpose instance driven by the AWS Nitro System and ARMv9 architecture. The instance provisions 192 dedicated physical cores across 192 vCPUs utilizing the ARM Neoverse-V3 microarchitecture operating at 3.3 GHz. The processor design includes 64 KB L1 data cache and 2 MB L2 cache per core, backed by 96 MB of shared L3 cache, along with hardware AES encryption support. Paired with the compute array is 768 GB of system memory, matching a balanced general-purpose allocation of 4.0 GB per core. In addition, the instance integrates 11,400 GB of local NVMe SSD instance storage and delivers 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, operating entirely without discrete GPU accelerators.

Benchmark evaluations demonstrate exceptional multi-core throughput and memory subsystem capacity. In multi-threaded CPU stress tests and PassMark multi-core evaluations, the server achieves top-tier scores, reinforced by high-throughput memory streaming exceeding 729 GB/s on large un-cached read operations and 327 GB/s on writes. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression reaches 1,933.56 GB/s, while database operations and Redis SET benchmarks show top-decile execution rates, exceeding 500 million operations per second. However, single-core processing reflects moderate performance, with stress-ng single-core metrics placing in the median 50 percent bracket. Natural language token generation benchmarks similarly demonstrate baseline CPU-only throughput, emphasizing that throughput gains rely on parallel execution rather than individual core clock speed.

The architectural design achieves qualitative cost efficiency by packing dense core counts and large-capacity NVMe storage into a single host envelope without requiring external storage attachments. This dense allocation allows data-intensive applications to minimize interconnect overhead and maintain high operational density. The hardware configuration is best matched for distributed caching layers, large-scale Redis deployments, localized NoSQL and relational database clusters, batch compression pipelines, static web serving clusters, and multi-tenant data processing jobs that benefit from massive core parallelism and fast local scratch storage.
description: Amazon Web Services m9gd.48xlarge is a general-purpose, Nitro-virtualized instance powered by 192 dedicated AWS ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 cores running at 3.3 GHz. Configured with a 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the instance provides 768 GB of system memory (4.0 GB per core) alongside 11,400 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and 100 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The server excludes hardware accelerators such as GPUs. Benchmark results position the server in the top tier for multi-core stress testing, memory bandwidth, PassMark database operations, and multi-threaded decompression, though single-core compute performance remains in the median range. Hardware-level cryptographic acceleration supports secure processing without compromising throughput. Delivering massive thread concurrency and dense on-host ephemeral storage, the hardware profile offers strong qualitative resource efficiency for parallel data processing pipelines, high-throughput caching tiers like Redis, distributed NoSQL databases, and intensive web serving workloads.
